answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a opal as the anchor of the cost. A oasis stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a haven holds the rep...
